tools.description: Create doors/windows from nonempty items in input order, each in its own transaction. position is the absolute world center {x, y, z} in millimetres: x/y select the nearest wall and are projected onto it, while z is the actual model center, not the bottom elevation. For example, a 2100 mm floor-level door uses z=1050. Pass z=0 only to request the catalog default height and sill/elevation offset. For a single swing door, openingDirection optionally selects push_left, push_right, pull_left or pull_right; other symbols reject that field. size is {x, y, z} for width/depth/height. Returned position and size are wall-adapted values. A position with no wall nearby or an unavailable product creates nothing. Repeated productIds create separate elements. Failures do not stop later items; results include index, productId and each outcome; applied is true only if every item succeeds, with total/succeeded/failed counts. Use items with one element for a single creation.

items.description: Doors/windows to create in order. Repeated productIds create separate elements.

openingDirection.description: Optional single swing door direction: push_left, push_right, pull_left or pull_right. Left/right follow the door/window convention relative to the door facing, not world axes. Omit to use the catalog default; do not use for other door/window types.

position.description: Absolute world center {x, y, z} in millimetres. x/y select the nearest wall and are projected onto it. z is the actual model center, not the bottom elevation: for a 2100 mm floor-level door use z=1050. Pass z=0 only to request the catalog default height and sill/elevation offset.

productId.description: Catalog productId of the door or window to create, as returned by get_defaults.

size.description: Omit to use the catalog dimensions.

tools.description: Read doors and windows in the current design: id, productId, position, rotation, size and openingDirection. openingDirection is push_left, push_right, pull_left or pull_right for a single swing door, and null for other symbols. Millimetres and radians; size is {x, y, z} for width/depth/height; position is an absolute world center {x, y, z} object. Omit ids to read everything.

ids.description: Door/window element IDs to read. Omit to read every door and window in the design.

tools.description: List the catalog product that each door/window type is created from: IWindow (standard window), frenchWindow, IBayWindow, singleDoor, doubleDoor and slidingDoor. Use the returned productId as the add tool's productId. Types without a product - door openings and cased openings, plus anything the catalog does not serve in this environment - are reported under skipped instead of being silently absent. size is {x, y, z} for width/depth/height.
Remove doors and windows by id and report which IDs were actually deleted. IDs that do not exist are reported instead of being retried.

ids.description: Door/window element IDs to remove. Duplicates are ignored.

tools.description: Apply nonempty items in order, each in its own transaction, to move, resize and/or change door/window opening directions and return each resulting state. openingDirection applies only to a single swing door and accepts push_left, push_right, pull_left or pull_right; the change updates its 2D opening symbol. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Position is the absolute world center {x, y, z}: x/y select the nearest wall and are projected onto it, while z is the actual model center and is clamped only to the host wall height range. size uses {x, y, z} for width/depth/height; only supplied axes change. Returned position and size are the adapted values. Rotation is derived from the wall and cannot be set. Millimetres, absolute values, within the allowed ranges. Repeated elementIds are applied sequentially. Failures do not stop later items. results include index, elementId and each outcome; applied is true only if every item succeeds, with total/succeeded/failed counts. Use items with one element for one edit.

items.description: Door/window changes to apply in order. Repeated elementIds are updated sequentially.

elementId.description: ID of the door/window element to change.

openingDirection.description: Change a single swing door to push_left, push_right, pull_left or pull_right. Left/right follow the door/window convention relative to the door facing, not world axes. Do not use for other door/window types.

position.description: Move the element using its absolute world center {x, y, z}. x/y select the nearest wall and are projected onto it; z is the actual model center, not the bottom elevation.

size.description: Absolute local dimensions in millimetres; only the supplied ones change.
